name: winnow
description: Fork of nom by a former nom maintainer, focused on ergonomics, imperative style, and documentation

license.comment: Cargo.toml `license = "MIT"`; crates.io lists MIT for every version.

approach.comment: Self-described as 'a byte-oriented, zero-copy, parser combinators library'.

implementation.comment: Only optional pure-Rust deps (memchr, anstream, anstyle, is_terminal_polyfill, terminal_size); no C/C++ in the tree.

documentation.comment: docs.rs doubles as the book: embedded `_tutorial` (chapters 0-8) and `_topic` special-topic modules.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 1.0.4 published 2026-07-13. Research reflects the 1.0.x API (0.5 -> 0.6/0.7 -> 1.0 changed error/result types, e.g. ModalResult, ContextError).

grammar-class.comment: Combinators impose no formal grammar class (per Assessment Guidelines); no documented PEG semantics.

grammar-definition.comment: Parsers are plain Rust functions `fn(&mut I) -> Result<O, E>` composed with combinators.

left-recursion.comment: `combinator::expression()` is a documented Pratt parser (prefix/infix/postfix with binding powers). Plain recursion into a left-recursive rule still loops; rewrite or use `expression`.

ambiguity-handling.comment: `alt` tries alternatives in order and returns the first success; `ErrMode::Backtrack` drives the retry.

backtracking.comment: `cut_err` converts a Backtrack error into `ErrMode::Cut` so `alt` stops trying alternatives; `backtrack_err` reverses it.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless over &str/&[u8] by default; also parses `&[T]`/`TokenSlice<T>` of user tokens (documented 'Lexing and Parsing' topic), so any token slice can be consumed.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: `combinator::expression()` Pratt builder (prefix/infix/postfix, associativity, binding power); gated on the default `parser` feature.

unicode-aware.comment: `&str` is a first-class Stream with `char` tokens (`AsChar`); byte-level `&[u8]` parsing is also available and recommended for speed.

input-types.comment: &str, &[u8], &[T]/TokenSlice<T>, plus user types implementing the `Stream` trait. No rope/text-buffer input.

streaming-partial-input.comment: `Partial<I>` wrapper + `ErrMode::Incomplete(Needed)`; ndjson example shows chunked buffering.

zero-copy.comment: Self-described as zero-copy; parsers return slices of the input (`take`, `take_while`, `Parser::take`).

span-tracking.comment: Opt-in via the `LocatingSlice` wrapper (implements `Location`); `Parser::span()`/`with_span()` yield `Range<usize>` byte offsets. No built-in line/column.

output-model.comment: Each parser returns an arbitrary user Rust type; no generic tree.

semantic-actions.comment: `.map()`, `.try_map()`, `.value()`, `.parse_to()` etc. on the `Parser` trait; or imperative code in a plain fn.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: No implicit skip rules; use `ascii::multispace0`, `delimited`, `preceded`, etc., or skip in a lexer when using token slices.

stateful-parsing.comment: `Stateful<I, S>` stream wrapper threads user state through all parsers.

error-recovery.comment: Only behind the `unstable-recover` feature (requires `std`): `Recoverable<I, E>` stream + `RecoverableParser::recoverable_parse` collect errors and resume; user chooses where/how to recover. Not stable API as of 1.0.4.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: `Recoverable` keeps a `Vec<E>` of collected errors (`into_parts()`); requires the `unstable-recover` feature. Without it, parsing stops at the first error.

expected-token-reporting.comment: No automatic expected-set. `ContextError` only carries `StrContext::Expected(..)` items the user attaches manually via `.context()`; not rounded up per guideline.

custom-error-types.comment: Error type is a generic parameter; implement `ParserError` (+ optional `AddContext`, `FromExternalError`). Built-ins: ContextError, TreeError, EmptyError, InputError.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Top-level `ParseError::offset()` gives a single byte offset; ranges require the user to add `with_span`/LocatingSlice themselves. No labelled secondary spans.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: Tutorial chapter 7 renders errors with annotate-snippets (dev-dependency); no first-party bridge crate, no ariadne/miette/codespan docs.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No tree reuse; `Partial` handles appended input, not edits.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: No CST; output is whatever the user builds (toml_edit builds its own lossless document on top).

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: No verified editor/LSP dependency found; Cargo uses winnow directly and via toml_edit, but that is not an editor.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: epage/parse-benchmarks-rs (maintainer-authored, includes competitors, reproducible; checked 2026-09-19, rustc 1.94.1): winnow 1.0.1 JSON parse 27 ms vs serde_json 18 ms (1.5x), nom 8 68 ms, chumsky 0.12 47 ms, pest 62 ms. Borderline top-tier/fast; treat with the usual maintainer-benchmark caution.

compile-time-impact.comment: Same benchmark: 1 s debug build for the winnow JSON parser (lowest of all parsers; nom 3 s, chumsky 5 s, lalrpop 12 s). Performance topic warns against returning deep `impl Parser` chains.

allocation-strategy.comment: Core works without `alloc` (no_std, zero-copy slices, `EmptyError`); `repeat`/`ContextError` need `alloc`.

generated-code-size.comment: Combinator library; no generated code. No source needed.

no-std-support.comment: `#![cfg_attr(all(not(feature = "std"), not(test)), no_std)]`; `std` and `alloc` are separate features (default = std, ascii, binary). Works with or without `alloc`.

msrv.comment: Cargo.toml `rust-version = "1.65.0"`; docs state a policy of supporting the last 6 months of Rust releases.

unsafe-usage.comment: No `forbid(unsafe_code)`; unsafe confined to `*_slice_unchecked` (`get_unchecked`) fast paths for &str/&[T] in stream/mod.rs (~10 occurrences).

proc-macro-reliance.comment: No proc-macro deps; `dispatch!`/`seq!` are declarative macros.

dependency-count.comment: All 5 direct deps are optional (memchr behind `simd`; anstream, anstyle, is_terminal_polyfill, terminal_size behind `debug`); the default feature set pulls in 0 dependencies.

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: pure Rust, no_std-capable, zero default deps; no explicit wasm CI target verified.

async-friendly.comment: Parsers are plain fns/closures (Send when captures are); `Partial` + `Incomplete` lets an async reader feed buffered chunks. No async-specific API.

crates-io-downloads.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; inflated by toml_edit/Cargo dependency chain.

maintenance-status.comment: Releases 2026-04, 2026-05, 2026-07; repo pushed 2026-09-17. Fork of nom 7 (nom is not superseded; both live).

documentation-quality.comment: 9-chapter tutorial, special topics (why, performance, partial, stateful, custom stream, custom errors, lexing), format cookbooks (JSON, INI, HTTP, s-expr, arithmetic), nom migration guide, plus full API docs.

notable-users.value: Cargo (direct + via toml_edit), toml_edit / toml, hcl-edit

bus-factor.comment: epage (2137 commits) is the sole active maintainer; Geal's 1808 commits are inherited nom history. Other contributors <100 commits each.
